title: Recommendation Engine
summary: A recommendation engine picks a handful of items out of millions in about 100 milliseconds. Scoring everything is too slow, so it works like a funnel. Cheap retrieval narrows millions of items to about a thousand candidates, a heavier model ranks those using fresh features, and business rules polish the final list. Every impression and click is logged and becomes training data for tomorrow's models.

walkthrough.title: Request recommendations
walkthrough.text: The app opens the home screen and asks for 20 items for user 42, with context like device, time of day, and the last item viewed.

walkthrough.title: Generate candidates
walkthrough.text: Several cheap retrievers run in parallel: an approximate-nearest-neighbour search over item embeddings near the user's embedding, 'because you watched X', and trending items. Together they return about 1,000 candidates.

walkthrough.title: Fetch features
walkthrough.text: The online feature store returns user features (recent clicks, preferences) and item features (CTR in the last hour, age, popularity) for every candidate.

walkthrough.title: Rank
walkthrough.text: A heavier model, such as a gradient-boosted tree or deep network, predicts each candidate's probability of click, watch, or purchase and combines them into one score.

walkthrough.title: Re-rank and filter
walkthrough.text: Business rules remove items already seen, out of stock, or blocked, add diversity so the page is not ten near-identical items, and blend in some exploration.

walkthrough.title: Return the page
walkthrough.text: The ranked list goes back to the app with a request ID, so every later click can be tied to exactly what was shown.

walkthrough.title: Log impressions and clicks
walkthrough.text: The app streams what was shown and what the user did. Items that were not clicked count as negative examples.

walkthrough.title: Retrain and refresh
walkthrough.text: Offline jobs join logged features with outcomes, retrain the models and embeddings, and publish new features and model versions after an A/B test.

data.label: Client App
responsibilities: Asks for recommendations per surface: home, 'more like this', email.
Logs exactly what was shown and in which position, not just clicks.
Shows a fallback (popular items) if the request is slow.

failureModes.impact: Models only see clicks, cannot learn what was ignored, and overrate popular items.
failureModes.mitigation: Log impressions on render with the requestId; monitor the click/impression join rate.
Client deadline with cached or popular fallback lists.

data.label: Recommendation Service

output.name: Ranked list
output.type: Top-n items with scores and explanations

responsibilities: Runs the funnel: retrieve, fetch features, rank, re-rank, within a ~100 ms budget.
Calls retrievers in parallel and drops any that miss their deadline.
Logs the exact features used, so training data matches serving (no training/serving skew).

failureModes.impact: p99 latency blows the page budget.
failureModes.mitigation: Rank fewer candidates under pressure; fall back to the retrieval order.
Popular items in the user's locale plus onboarding questions; learn quickly from early clicks.

data.label: Candidate Retrieval
responsibilities: Finds items whose embeddings are close to the user's embedding in a few milliseconds.
Mixes sources (similar items, trending, followed creators) so no single signal dominates.
Keeps the index fresh so new items can appear within minutes.

failureModes.scenario: New items have no embedding yet
failureModes.impact: Fresh content never gets recommended (item cold start).
failureModes.mitigation: Content-based embeddings from title, image, and text at upload; reserved exploration slots.

failureModes.impact: Users only see more of the same and engagement slowly drops.
failureModes.mitigation: Diversity-aware retrieval sources and exploration traffic.

data.label: Online Feature Store
responsibilities: Serves precomputed and streaming features with low latency.
Uses the same feature definitions offline and online, so the model sees consistent inputs.
Updates real-time signals like 'clicked in the last 5 minutes' from the event stream.

failureModes.impact: Stale features; trending items are missed.
failureModes.mitigation: Freshness metrics per feature with alerts; models trained to tolerate missing values.

failureModes.impact: The model performs well offline but poorly in production.
failureModes.mitigation: Log the served features and train on those logs.

data.label: Ranking & Re-ranking

output.name: Final list
output.type: Top 20 after scoring, filtering, and diversity rules

responsibilities: Predicts several outcomes (click, watch time, purchase) and blends them into one score.
Applies filters: already seen, unavailable, age-restricted, blocked creators.
Re-ranks for diversity and freshness, and reserves slots for exploration.

failureModes.mitigation: Blend in longer-term signals (watch time, returns, surveys) and guardrail metrics in A/B tests.
Shadow scoring, canary traffic, and automatic rollback on metric drops.

data.label: Event Stream

input.name: Events
input.type: { requestId, userId, itemId, position, action, ts }

responsibilities: Collects impressions and interactions from every client.
Joins outcomes to the impression and its logged features.
Updates real-time counters such as item CTR in the last hour.

failureModes.mitigation: Bot filtering before training; anomaly detection on click patterns.

failureModes.impact: Some clicks are labelled as non-clicks.
failureModes.mitigation: Use a watermark window before labelling negatives.

data.label: Offline Training

output.name: Artifacts
output.type: New ranking model, item embeddings, batch features

responsibilities: Retrains models and embeddings daily or continuously.
Validates offline metrics before a version reaches an A/B test.
Backfills batch features into the online store.

failureModes.impact: The model only learns about items it already chose to show.
failureModes.mitigation: Exploration traffic and position-bias correction in training.

failureModes.impact: Great offline metrics, useless in production.
failureModes.mitigation: Point-in-time correct joins: only use feature values known at impression time.
